newsitem.title: USA: Host of TV talk show says she was not embarrassed.
newsitem.headline: Host of TV talk show says she was not embarrassed.

text.p: Talk show host Jenny Jones told a court Thursday her programme on same-sex secret admirers, after which one guest killed another, was not "ambush television."
She also testified that she was not embarrassed about the premise of the show, which was taped on March 6, 1995, but never aired.

Jones was called to the witness stand by lawyers defending Jonathan Schmitz, 26, accused of first-degree murder in the shotgun death of Scott Amedure, 32, three days after Amedure revealed his homosexual attraction to Schmitz during a taping of the "Jenny Jones" show. Schmitz, who told the audience watching the show that he was heterosexual, called police to turn himself in after the shooting.
Defence attorney Fred Gibson asked Jones if the show was "ambush television."

He quizzed her on an apology she read on the air several days after the shooting in which she referred to the show in question as one involving "secret admirers." She admitted under questioning that the topic was really "same-sex secret crushes" even though her statement did not use that phrase.
"Were you embarrassed about the topic or plot of that particular show?" Gibson asked her.

Asked why she did not reveal the true nature of the show in her apology, she said, "because the premise of the show was that it was a surprise." When Gibson suggested she had not "set the record straight" with her viewers, Jones said she did not write the statement she read on the air.

She also testified that none of her producers advised her about anything Schmitz did not want to be revealed on the air and said the type of programme on which the two men appeared was known around her office as a "crush show."

The blonde TV star appeared in an off-white business suit, aswering questions in a quiet voice. Among other things she revealed that her given name was Jenny Stronski but said she is now legally Jenny Jones.

Schmitz alleges he was humiliated in front of the studio audience. That experience, combined with manic depression and Graves disease, a thyroid condition that can have emotional side effects, contributed to his buying a 12-gauge shotgun and shooting Amedure twice in the chest, defence attorneys say.

Before Jones took the stand, Schmitz's father, Allyn, testified that his son had a history of alcohol abuse and suicide attempts but before his appearance on the TV show had turned his life around with a new job.

He was excited about going on the show, the father said, and speculated on which woman -- but never any man -- might be his secret admirer. He said before the show was taped that he would be "knee deep" in women after it aired, the father said.

Although Schmitz is charged with first-degree murder, the jury could find him guilty of second-degree murder, manslaughter or reckless discharge (of a weapon) causing death. If convicted of the most serious offence, Schmitz could be sentenced to life in prison without possibility of parole.
